chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram who dies, what is done with him? He narrated to me: 'That Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) died at al-awa while in ihram, along with al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him). With al-Husayn (peace be upon him) were Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas and Abd Allah ibn Ja'far. So they did with him as they do with the deceased: they covered his face and did not apply perfume to him.' He said: 'And that is in the book of Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who dies while in the state of ihram regarding burial and perfume?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the ruling for a deceased pilgrim in ihram by citing the historical precedent of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hasan, whose body was treated as a regular corpse with the face covered and perfume avoided to preserve the state of ihram. The narration confirms this practice through the authority of the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), reinforcing the continuity of prophetic tradition in Shia jurisprudence regarding funeral rites for those in a sacred state.
